title: When Tokyo's Doctors Decided to Make Their Own Thermometers
conflicts: Timing of the thermometer shortage: Terumo's 2021 release ties it to the outbreak of war in 1914, NetIB-News (2020) says German thermometers became hard to obtain after the war; the story attributes the 1914 timing to the company's history. Who initiated: Terumo names engineer Eiji Takeuchi and Dr Miozo Sasagawa as initiators with Kitasato chairing, rather than Kitasato as sole founder; the story follows Terumo and NetIB-News. No outcome numbers conflict.
notes: Funding changed from the slate's 'mixed' to 'unknown': capital of 500,000 yen is documented but not who subscribed it. Hiroshi Morishita's board role rests on NetIB-News alone. Kitasato's remark about commerce is paraphrased from a second-hand Japanese report, not quoted. terumo.com and terumo.co.jp block automated requests, so Terumo is cited via terumois.com and terumomedical.com.
